newsitem.title: UK: European bourses fall sharply, hit by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: European bourses fall sharply, hit by Wall St.

text.p: European bourses fell sharply on Wednesday as Wall Street was hit by profit-taking at the opening after its second record close in a row .
And on currency markets, the dollar ran out of steam after earlier strengthening on growing speculation about an increase in U.S. interest rates.
The disappointing showing on equity markets followed an unsettled day on Tuesday when European shares backtracked after roaring to new record trading highs in early business.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, dipped by 0.5 percent, unsettled by Wall Street's negative opening. London's FTSE index has closed at new peaks for the previous six sessions.
Dealers said they were encouraged that the market had not made even bigger losses, given the 137-points surge in the last six trading sessions.
"There are still a lot of shorts out there," said one dealer. "We could see one more final squeeze before we get a correction," said one dealer.

European sentiment was shaken as the Dow Jones industrial average fell in early trading on Wednesday as investors grabbed some profits after hitting a record close for the second session in a row on Tuesday.

"So far all you can surmise is that this is normal profit-taking after the move we had over the last few days," said Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane. He said investors were cautious ahead of this Friday's producer price index and next week's consumer price index.
The Dow was down 15 points at 7071 while declines led advancing issues by about 12 to seven.
Despite the Dow's recent bull run, the overall U.S. market was nervous because of speculation that the Federal Reserve might be planning an interest rate increase.
Investors were worried about Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's warnings recently that stocks could be overvalued and that the central bank might raise short-term interest rates.
In Paris, stocks fell 1.57 percent, weighed down by worries about long-term interest rate trends that fuelled profit-taking, traders said.

"A lot of analysts are unclear where the market's going from here," said Olivier Blitz at IFF Bourse. The bourse's underlying upward trend looked intact, particularly if the futures contract held above 2,670 points. If it broke that level, he said, a significant correction might take place.

Against the trend, shares in Lafarge rose 1.63 percent to 373.50 francs at one point after the group reported net attributable profit of 1.85 billion francs ($321 million), which was well received by the market.
In Frankfurt, shares on the computerised IBIS index were down 1.45 percent because of the weakening dollar and the poor opening on Wall Street.

Floor trading had earlier closed showing losses of 1.31 percent. The market was weakened as chemicals group Hoechst AG fell 3.25 marks, more than four percent, to 71.95 after it shelved plans to list its HMR Marion Roussel unit.

In currencies, the dollar was up by nearly a yen and half a pfennig in morning trade on interest rates speculation but weakened. By mid-afternoon it was back to the levels seen in late trade on Tuesday against the mark.

The US central bank's policy-making Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on March 25 and ebbing and flowing speculation about a rise in interest rates after the meeting has buffeted the dollar this week.
The Fed's latest economic assessment, or Beige Book, will be presented to the FOMC and is due for release at 1900 GMT today.
Much of the attention on foreign exchanges centred on sterling, which was hit by a series of comments from the deputy-governor of the Bank of England, Howard Davies, in Japan.

Davies said the central bank was still in favour of a quarter-point rise in British interest rates but he added that currency forward rates showed the market was discounting a future decline in sterling.
At one point, the pound was at a 5-1/2-month low at $1.5899, down from $1.6053 late on Tuesday.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7020 marks and 122.58 yen compared with 1.7038 marks and 121.82 yen in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS 1600 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 24.4 points at 4,419.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 44.45 points at 2,641.70.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down down 45.19 points at 3,415.40.
PRECIOUS METALS 1600 GMT
Gold was fixed in the afternon at $351.40 an ounce unchanged from the close on Tuesday. Silver was at $5.24, up three cents. ($ = 5.760 French Francs)
